task.title: Bring Workbench into the repository as desktop/
task.description:
Bring the Workbench source in under `desktop/` and make it build against this checkout instead of a pinned clone.

Depends on the decision task; do not start before it is answered.

## Shape

    desktop/
      package.json      electron-builder config, the app's version
      src/main/         window, views, IPC, the supervisor that runs one
                        `workbook serve` per imported project
      src/renderer/     shell UI
      scripts/          staging, packaging hooks, its own checks
      assets/           icons

Roughly 250 KB of source and 23 commits, brought over with `git subtree add --prefix=desktop` so the history survives rather than arriving as one squashed import.

## The part that is not just a move

`scripts/build-workbook.sh` currently reads a repository and ref out of `package.json`, clones it into `build/workbook-src`, and delegates to this repository's own `scripts/install.sh` so the binary is stamped exactly as an official source install is. In-tree it builds from the checkout it already sits in, and the pin disappears.

`WORKBOOK_REPO` and `WORKBOOK_REF` should survive as overrides — building the desktop app against some other revision is still worth being able to do — but the default stops being a clone.

## Landing this before it moves

#131 and #132 delete rather than migrate three pieces of Workbench that exist only because the board had no dark mode: a 10.6 KB generated override sheet (`board-dark.css`), its generator (`scripts/generate-board-dark.js`), and a per-project dark-ramp derivation (`src/main/boardtheme.js`). Landing them first is what makes this a smaller move.
